evidence: docs/UNITS.md (257 lines) covers all five planned sections: internal storage rules, helper naming convention, display/labeling policy, type-safety roadmap, and migration expectations. The document is cross-linked from README.md and docs/scientific_inventory.md.

AC #1 (consistent field/helper naming convention): The Canonical Quantity Taxonomy table defines patterns (_mg_n_total, _mg_p_total, _mg_c_total, _mg_total, _meq_total, _per_l variants) with examples. Helper Naming Policy §1-2 prescribes concentration-helper and pure-conversion-helper naming with explicit volume_l parameter requirements. A migration table maps all 11 legacy ProcessParams half-saturation fields to their canonical concentration-based target names.

AC #2 (display policy written before refactors): Snapshot/API/TUI Display Policy §1-6 defines scientific element-basis as default, ion-style as opt-in, TDS/conductivity must carry 'Est.' prefix, GH/KH show derivation basis, and precision defaults per quantity. A rename table maps 6 current snapshot fields (tan_mg_l, nh3_mg_l, nitrite_mg_l, nitrate_mg_l, phosphate_mg_l, dissolved_inorganic_carbon_mg_l) to canonical field names and labels.

AC #3 (explicit enough to prevent semantic drift): The policy bans bare '_mg_l' for N/P/C chemistry, requires element-basis in every field name, defines save-file serialization rules (total-based, no duplicated concentration mirrors), and requires explicit migration handling (serde aliases or schema-version bump) for field renames.

Conversion factors are scientifically correct: NO₃⁻/N = 62/14 ≈ 4.43, NO₂⁻/N = 46/14 ≈ 3.29, PO₄³⁻/P = 95/31 ≈ 3.06, NH₃/N = 17/14 ≈ 1.21. TAN exception correctly forbids a single fixed ion-multiplier since TAN = NH₃ + NH₄⁺ with pH/temperature-dependent speciation.

Cross-reference with codebase confirmed: WaterState fields (water.rs) already comply with _total naming. SourceWaterProfile fields (source_water.rs) already comply with _per_l naming. All 6 ambiguous snapshot fields and 11 legacy parameter fields are correctly identified for downstream rename work. TUI chemistry screen (chemistry.rs:23-27) uses bare 'mg/L' labels as documented.

Downstream beads are explicitly assigned: tanksim-6e5.2.2 owns concentration helpers and parameter renames; tanksim-6e5.2.7 owns snapshot/API field renames, display toggle, and TDS/conductivity relabeling. The policy provides unambiguous rename targets for both.
findings_or_gaps: Minor: TDS and conductivity rename targets (estimated_tds_7_ion_mg_per_l, estimated_conductivity_us_cm) appear only in §4 prose, not in the consolidated snapshot rename table in §2. Adding them to that table would give tanksim-6e5.2.7 a single authoritative rename checklist instead of requiring cross-referencing two sections.

Minor: The NH₄⁺/N conversion factor (18/14 ≈ 1.29) is absent from the canonical conversion constants list, even though it appeared in the plan's assumptions. The TAN exception note explains why a single TAN-as-ion factor is wrong, but the individual NH₄⁺/N factor is still useful for speciated ion-display (e.g., showing NH₄⁺ fraction as mg NH₄⁺/L). Documenting it alongside NH₃/N = 17/14 would be more complete.

Observation: The prior docs_validation stage returned empty evidence, findings, and follow-up arrays with an 'approved' outcome — effectively a rubber-stamp. A substantive validation would have strengthened confidence; this review compensates.

Observation: The policy does not address DOC and DON display naming. Current snapshot omits these, but if they are added later (plausible for a debugging or advanced view), the convention should extend naturally. The existing rules cover them implicitly (_mg_c_per_l, _mg_n_per_l) but an explicit note would prevent ambiguity.
follow_up_or_amendments: Optional: Consolidate all snapshot/API field renames (including TDS/conductivity) into one table in UNITS.md so tanksim-6e5.2.7 has a single checklist. This is a quality-of-life improvement, not a blocker.
Optional: Add NH₄⁺/N = 18/14 ≈ 1.29 to the canonical conversion constants, noting it is used only for speciated ion-display, not for TAN-as-a-whole.
No code changes are expected from this bead — all implementation belongs to downstream beads (tanksim-6e5.2.2, tanksim-6e5.2.7). The policy is complete and ready to unblock those dependents.
